The main takeaway from our work is that

the DT-diaphorases are the major enzymes responsible for the detoxification of aziridinybenzoquinones, and their inactivation leads to increased cytotoxicity under aerobic as well as hypoxic conditions.
DT-diapharase plays a protective role by catalyzing two-electron reduction of aziridines, thereby avoiding the formation of reactive intermediates that cause oxidative stress.

the cytotoxicity of trenimon is modulated by the DT-diaphorases under both aerobic and hypoxic conditions, and the cytotoxic mechanism is likely to involve macromolecular aliphatic alkylations under hypoxic conditions and oxidative stress under aerobic condition.
